objective: Design, train, and score through the benchmark's own harness a first genuinely trained data-driven RANS correction model for the closure-challenge benchmark, to be measured against the versioned RANS-identity reference floor (overall 0.1036) and the recorded rank-4 target (overall 0.0779), neither of which this proposal claims to beat in advance
rationale: This is queued, separate from the completed reference-floor measurement (r3-closure-challenge-rans-floor), because the two have fundamentally different cost profiles and conflating them understates the real work. The reference floor was zero-ML and measured in under a second. A genuinely trained baseline is a MULTI-DAY project, and the gating factor is not compute: the benchmark's own data is small (about 390 MB per GitHub, 1.3 GB uncompressed) and this host has 16 CPU cores idle enough to fit a scikit-learn-class model in minutes once features exist. The gate is three specific pieces of engineering discipline, none of which is bought back by more core-minutes: (1) FEATURE ENGINEERING DISCIPLINE -- the RANS fields alone are not enough; a defensible entry needs invariant, non-dimensionalized inputs (the field's own literature standard is a tensor-basis / invariant feature set, e.g. local velocity-gradient invariants, wall distance, turbulence intensity, built so a model trained at one Reynolds number and geometry generalizes to a held-out one, which is explicitly what this benchmark's train/test split is designed to test). (2) INVARIANT AND TENSOR-BASIS FEATURES specifically, because the benchmark's design philosophy is stated as testing Reynolds-number generalization and geometry generalization; naive raw-coordinate or raw-velocity features will not generalize across the held-out cases and would produce a number that looks trained but is not defensible. (3) TRAIN AND VALIDATION HYGIENE against the one binding rule of this challenge, carried forward here explicitly because it is a real constraint on any work under this proposal: it is strictly forbidden to train or validate on any of the 8 named test cases (alpha_15_13929_4048, alpha_15_13929_2024, alpha_05_4071_4048, alpha_05_4071_2024, AR_1_Ret_360, AR_3_Ret_360, AR_14_Ret_180, NASA_2DWMH); a violation automatically withdraws the submission. Training data available without touching those 8 cases: CBFS13700, PH_Breuer, PHLL10595 (single-variation cases), the remaining Parm_PH_29 periodic-hill alpha/Reynolds combinations not in the test list, and the DUCT aspect ratios not in the test list (AR_1_Ret_180, AR_3_Ret_180, AR_5_Ret_180, AR_7_Ret_180, AR_10_Ret_180). No number is forecast for what a trained model would score; the recorded rank-4 target (0.0779) and the measured reference floor (0.1036) are stated here only as the two fixed points a future measurement should be reported against, not as a target this proposal claims to reach.

cost_basis: estimate, not measured: no training run has been attempted. 60 core-minutes is a rough order-of-magnitude guess at the model-FITTING step alone (a scikit-learn-class regressor such as gradient-boosted trees on an estimated 10^5-10^6 training samples across the non-test cases, with a modest hyperparameter search on this host's cores), and should not be read as the cost of the project. The real cost is the feature-engineering and train/validation-hygiene effort described in the rationale, which is measured in engineering days, not core-minutes, and is not reflected in this field at all
expected_knowledge_gain: Either a first honestly-measured trained-model score on this benchmark, reported through its own harness whatever the number turns out to be, or a specific, named account of where a first attempt fails (feature set, generalization gap, or leakage risk) -- either outcome is more valuable than no attempt, but neither should be assumed before the work is done
gating_factors: feature engineering discipline: raw RANS fields are not sufficient inputs on their own
invariant and tensor-basis features: required for the Reynolds-number and geometry generalization the benchmark's split is designed to test
train and validation hygiene: the 8 named test cases must never be touched during training or validation, on penalty of automatic withdrawal
binding_rule: Strictly forbidden to train or validate on any of the 8 named test cases (alpha_15_13929_4048, alpha_15_13929_2024, alpha_05_4071_4048, alpha_05_4071_2024, AR_1_Ret_360, AR_3_Ret_360, AR_14_Ret_180, NASA_2DWMH). A violation automatically withdraws the submission per the benchmark's own rules.
launch_prompt: Do not skip to a training run. First: (1) design an invariant, non-dimensional input feature set (local RANS velocity-gradient invariants, wall distance, turbulence intensity) following the tensor-basis convention standard in the ML-RANS literature; (2) parse only the training-eligible cases the repo ships (CBFS13700, PH_Breuer, PHLL10595, the non-test Parm_PH_29 alpha/Re variations, the non-test DUCT aspect ratios) into that feature set, never touching the 8 named test cases; (3) fit a plain scikit-learn regressor (start with gradient-boosted trees, not a neural network) predicting the DNS/LES correction from the RANS-derived features; (4) interpolate predictions onto evaluation_points() for each test case and score with the unmodified closure_challenge.score(), following the same pattern sdk/scripts/run_closure_challenge_evidence.py already demonstrates for the zero-ML floor; (5) report whatever number results, measured against both the reference floor (0.1036) and the rank-4 target (0.0779), even if it is far from either. Budget this as a multi-day effort across sessions, not a single overnight run.
